## Web Search and JSON Schema with Mistral Agents

The Agents API offers web search as a connector, enabling developers to combine Mistral models with diverse, up-to-date information from web search, reputable news, and other sources. Web_search and web_search_premium work with the Conversations API (/v1/conversations) and the Agents API.

### Structured Output Support

Mistral's API supports structured outputs via a response_format field that can take a json_schema configuration. Custom Structured Outputs allow you to ensure the model provides an answer in a very specific JSON format by supplying a clear JSON schema.

### Combining Web Search with JSON Schema

Passing RESPONSE_SCHEMA via completionArgs.responseFormat enforces the JSON structure at the API level, so the recommendation field is always a valid connector name and the output is always parseable without regex. This demonstrates that you can use response_format with json_schema while the agent uses connectors like web_search.

In practice, you would configure an agent with the web_search connector tool in your agent definition, and then specify the response_format with json_schema in the completion_args to ensure structured output from your web search queries.

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. content.text:
Yes — an agent can combine the built-in `web_search` (or `web_search_premium`) connector with structured JSON output, but only through the **Agents/Conversations API**, not Chat Completions.

Key points:
- `web_search` and `web_search_premium` only work with the Conversations API and the Agents API — they are explicitly **not supported** in the Chat Completions API, because Chat Completions responses don't include the search-result references the tool needs ([Websearch docs](https://docs.mistral.ai/agents/connectors/websearch)).
- Structured outputs (`response_format` with `json_object` or a `json_schema`) are a standard `completion_args`/chat-completion feature ([JSON Mode](https://docs.mistral.ai/studio/conversations/structured-output/json_mode), [Custom Structured Outputs](https://docs.mistral.ai/studio-api/conversations/structured-output/custom)).
- When you create an agent, you attach tools (e.g., `web_search`) in the agent definition and set `completion_args` for things like temperature and — per the sampler-arguments description in the Agents docs — response formatting ([Agents & Conversations](https://docs.mistral.ai/agents/agents)). So a `web_search`-enabled agent can be configured with a `response_format` json_schema so its final answer is returned as structured JSON while it still performs web searches as an intermediate step.

Caveat: none of the docs I checked explicitly spell out this combination with a worked example or call out edge-case limitations (e.g., how references/citations get merged into the JSON schema output) — I only found supporting evidence, not a page that documents the combination end-to-end. If this is going into production, I'd recommend testing it directly (e.g., via the DeepWiki/connector cookbook pattern) rather than relying solely on the docs.

- [Build a Database Advisor Agent with the DeepWiki Connector (TypeScript) — Mistral AI Cookbook](https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/cookbooks/mistral-connectors-database-advisor-agent-01-connectors-management)
